title: Warmup cohort sequencing and pin cheatsheet
content:
Notes-to-self: quick reference for warmup sequencing, small-cohort pins, and lightweight rollback criteria. This is a working scratchpad — mix of heuristics, commands, and unresolved questions. For an official playbook, this needs cleanup and linking to runbooks (SRE).

Context and goal:
- We want a low-friction release pattern for model/model-variant swaps that minimizes user-visible regressions and cost spikes. Focus on short warmup cohorts that exercise different query shapes (short prompts, multi-turn chat, embeddings bursts).
- Primary constraints: p95 latency SLOs, per-token cost delta budget, and quality regressions tracked via small prompt set and synthetic asserts.

Principles (quick):
- Warmup cohorts should be sequenced by client impact and query shape, not just % of traffic.
- Start with non-critical, low-rate clients (background tasks, batch jobs), then low-latency tolerant interactive cohorts, then general population.
- Use short pin windows (10–30m) for early cohorts to catch regressions quickly; extend to 2–6 hours for wider cohorts before full cutover.
- Always keep an automatic fallback mapping to a nearby variant (same family, lower perf but safe).

Cohort sequencing template (example):
1) Shadow warmers (0% but mirrored): 15–30m run to validate model cold-start behavior without impacting traffic. Observe KV cache warmups and memory growth.
2) Batch / async jobs cohort (~0.1%): 10–30m. These are cheapest and exercise long-context usages. Watch for token cost deltas.
3) Canary interactive-1 (internal beta clients / test apps) (~0.5%): 10–30m. Focus on p50/p95 latency and functional correctness checks.
4) Canary interactive-2 (small external cohort, 1–2%): 30–120m. Broader query shapes. Increase observability granularity.
5) Regional ramp (per-region, +5% increments): 1–6 hours per step depending on signals.
6) Global traffic split to 100% with staged unpin/unlock and monitoring.

Pin rules & durations:
- Pin key: when a client is pinned to a model version, the routing system should preserve the pin for the configured window and also allow safe eviction if errors exceed thresholds.
- Default pin window for warmup cohorts: 20 minutes. For production ramps, pin windows = 2 hours.
- If client-specific SLAs require linger, use sticky pins with TTL 24h but gated behind opt-in.

Signals to watch (primary telemetry):
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 token latency, and generation tail latency (last token).
- Errors: model runtime errors, OOMs, decoder exceptions, and rate limit bursts.
- Quality regressions: top-10 prompt set score diffs (BLEU / ROUGE / task-specific heuristics or eval harness).
- Cost: tokens per request (median) and per-minute token throughput; watch for >10% increase vs baseline during cohort.
- Resource: GPU memory growth, swap usage, host CPU steal.
- Cold-starts: requests that observe >1.5x baseline latency on first request after idle period.

Quick alert thresholds (starter):
- p95 latency increase >25% over baseline for >5 minutes -> pause ramp to previous % and notify oncall.
- Error rate >1% absolute increase for 5 minutes or >300% relative for 3 minutes -> immediate rollback to pinned fallback.
- Cost per-token increase >20% sustained for 10 minutes -> investigate quantization/beam changes.
- Quality check failure: if any of the critical 25 prompt set triggers flagged outputs (explained below) -> gate expansion until manual review.

Quality checks (mini-eval harness):
- Keep a curated set of 25 prompts representing: auth flows, short Q/A, code completions, multi-turn clarifications, embeddings similarity edge cases.
- For each prompt, run baseline variant and candidate variant and compute simple diffs: token-length delta, log-prob mean delta, and one heuristic score (task-specific). Flag if score drops beyond threshold.
- Automation: job runs every 5 minutes during ramp and posts summary to #releases. If any prompt fails, automatically hold expansion.

Rollback / fallback mapping:
- fallback candidate: map to previous stable model variant (same quantization family if possible). Keep mapping table in runtime-config: model_x -> fallback_model_y.
- automatic rollback rules: if auto-alert triggers (see thresholds) hold and route 100% of pinned traffic to fallback for 15 minutes, then re-evaluate.
- manual rollback: oncall + release owner decision; note reason, time, and telemetry pointers.

Preflight checklist (pre-launch, tick boxes):
- [ ] Smoke test for endpoints (postman/quick curl): sanity generate and embeddings.
- [ ] Run warmup shadow traffic for 30m and verify memory/time series trend lines.
- [ ] Ensure small-eval harness passes (25 prompts) with zero critical failures.
- [ ] Confirm fallback mapping exists and is validated.
- [ ] Notify owners and oncall 30 minutes prior via Slack (channel: #release-alerts).
- [ ] Update runbook with the rollout ID and expected windows.

Post-launch quick audits (first 6 hours):
- Hour 0–1: high-frequency checks: p50/p95, errors, eval harness.
- Hour 1–3: spot-check real user sessions for hallucinations / misalignments.
- Hour 3–6: cost drift analysis and sample outputs by region.
- Capture at least 3 incidents if any regression found, attach request ids and sample outputs.

Operational snippets (commands/queries):
- Lightweight trace query (CLI):
  rwi telemetry query "model=ml-candidate and env=prod" --windows 15m --metrics p95_latency,error_rate > outputs.csv
- SQL-ish for small-eval pass rate (pseudo):
  SELECT variant, count(*) as checks, sum(pass::int) as passed, passed/checks as pass_rate FROM eval_runs WHERE rollout_id='RR-2026-03-12-gg' GROUP BY variant;
- Rollback trigger Slack template: 
  [ROLLBACK] rollout RR-2026-03-12-gg: auto-triggered due to p95>25% over baseline. Actioning fallback -> <fallback_model>. Oncall: @oncall-ml

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to fold client-specific quality tolerances into the pin heuristic? (ex: some customers accept 5% quality delta for cost savings)
- Can we do a rolling cache-warmup that pre-populates KV for top-N prefixes to reduce first-traffic instability? (prototype idea)
- Need a lightweight synthetic load generator for regional long-tail prompts — file an infra ticket.
- Should shadow warmers be counted toward customer quotas? probably not; need gating in billing.

Notes about sequencing rationale (why this diverges from standard canary):
- Traditional canaries move by % of traffic; that often mixes query shapes and hides regressions in tails. Sequencing by client and shape isolates risk and allows targeted rollback without global impact.
- Short pin windows early force quick detection; long sticky pins later reduce churn for stateful clients.

Last-minute heuristics I found useful in practice:
- Use 'heartbeat sampling' requests every 5m from each pinned client to detect silent slowdowns due to cache evictions.
- Shadow run must log memory allocations per request to detect leak patterns early.
- For embeddings-heavy workloads, watch for 2x throughput drop on CPU hosts (signals quantization fallback or data-path regression).

If I get time: convert this into a small plugin for the Console rollout UI that presents the sequence and auto-populates the ramp steps. For now, drop notes here and iterate.

Slack refs: #release-alerts, #runtime-observability, @oncall-ml

-- Priya (working draft)
